html:
The Central Kalahari Game Reserve, set up in 1961 partly as a home for the San, was largely emptied of its San people when the government moved them out in 1997 and 2002.

The San, hunter-gatherers whose ancestors lived in southern Africa long before farmers came, had hunted and gathered there for generations. The government said they should join modern life and get services in new settlements outside, while critics said diamonds and tourism were the real reasons.

In 2006 the High Court ruled the removals unlawful, but the government let only some return and limited their hunting and water. The case drew world attention to the San, the first people of Botswana and Namibia, and to the price of diamond-era development.
sum: The Central Kalahari Game Reserve, set up in 1961 partly as a home for the San, was largely emptied of its San people when the government moved them out in 1997 and 2002.
